claims.text: Local Cu segregation governs the onset and progression of the phase transition in FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Cu has a considerably lower melting point than Fe, Ni, Cr, and Co.
Cu-rich regions form premelting liquid domains that nucleate further melting throughout the particles.
The nanoparticles initially have a crystalline and compositionally homogeneous FeNiCrCoCu structure.
Heating is conducted incrementally under an inert atmosphere while structural and compositional changes are monitored.
An inert atmosphere prevents oxidation during heating.
Particles with standard and deliberately varied Cu content are compared using identical heating rates.
Elemental fluctuations or segregation produce local Cu-rich domains with lower local melting thresholds.
Small compositional inhomogeneities promote local Cu enrichment.
Cu-rich pockets melt at lower temperatures than the surrounding alloy and form liquid regions.
The first liquid regions increase atomic mobility and lattice disorder in adjacent material.
Increased mobility and disorder propagate melting heterogeneously through the nanoparticles.
Premelting liquid domains first emerge at locally Cu-concentrated regions.
The domains appear near or slightly above the melting point of Cu.
Liquid domains progressively coalesce and propagate until the nanoparticles melt completely.
The room-temperature baseline is fully solid, crystalline, compositionally uniform, and shows no premature melting.
The proposed behavior applies under inert, uniformly heated conditions, whereas thermal spikes or oxidation may alter transition progression.
Spatially resolved in situ microscopy, diffraction, and elemental mapping can test whether melting onset correlates with Cu enrichment.
Increasing or homogenizing Cu content should produce a corresponding shift in melting behavior.
Uniform liquid onset without spatial correlation to Cu enrichment, or no melting shift after intentional modification of Cu segregation, would refute the hypothesis.
